configuration_examples.overview: Complete examples demonstrating how to create REST connector configuration files for different types of APIs and scenarios.

example.name: simple_public_api
example.title: Simple Public API (No Authentication)
example.description: SpaceX API - a public REST API with no authentication required. Demonstrates basic endpoint mapping with various data types.
example.configuration: { "$connector_name": "spacex-api-connector", "$connector_label": "SpaceX API", "$connector_description": "Connector for SpaceX public REST API - provides access to rockets, launches, capsules, and more", "$hostname": "https://api.spacexdata.com", "$authentication": { "type": "none" }, "$tables": { "ROCKETS": { "$path": ["/v4/rockets"], "id": "VARCHAR,$key", "name": "VARCHAR", "type": "VARCHAR", "active": "BOOLEAN", "stages": "INTEGER", "boosters": "INTEGER", "cost_per_launch": "BIGINT", "success_rate_pct": "INTEGER", "first_flight": "DATE", "country": "VARCHAR", "company": "VARCHAR", "height[]": {"meters":"VARCHAR","feet":"VARCHAR"}, "diameter[]": {"meters":"VARCHAR","feet":"VARCHAR"}, "mass[]": {"kg":"INTEGER","lb":"INTEGER"}, "engines[]": {"number":"INTEGER","type":"VARCHAR","version":"VARCHAR","layout":"VARCHAR"}, "flickr_images": "VARCHAR" } } }

decision.reason: String UUID used as primary key
True/false value
Large integer value (50 million)
Date string in YYYY-MM-DD format
Fixed-structure nested objects marked with [] suffix. Connector automatically flattens these into separate columns with dot notation. For example, height[] creates columns: height.meters, height.feet
Array - stored as JSON string

example.name: api_with_authentication
example.title: API with API Key Authentication
example.description: Example API requiring API Key authentication. The $authentication block uses the uniform headers-array format. The "name" field is the connection-property key (what CP4D asks the user to fill in) and also the $var placeholder used inside the "value" template.

decision.reason: API requires API Key in Authorization header
Connection-property key. CP4D will prompt the user for "API Key" and store it under this key.
Header value template. $api_key is replaced at runtime with the user-supplied connection property.
Numeric ID used as primary key
ISO 8601 date-time string
Fixed-structure nested object with [] suffix. Creates columns: profile.first_name, profile.last_name, profile.avatar_url

example.name: api_without_natural_key
example.title: API Response Without Natural Unique Identifier
example.description: Polish National Bank API - returns data without natural unique IDs. Demonstrates using synthetic ROWID as primary key.

decision.reason: No natural unique identifier in response - synthetic key added
decision.note: Connector automatically generates unique ROWID for each row

decision.reason: Date string in YYYY-MM-DD format
Monetary value - use DECIMAL for precision

example.name: oauth2_authentication
example.title: API with OAuth2 Bearer Token
example.description: Example API using OAuth2 Bearer Token authentication. The bearer_token connection property is placed into the Authorization header via the value template "Bearer $bearer_token".
example.note: User must obtain OAuth2 bearer token through their OAuth2 flow before creating connection. Token refresh is not currently supported by the connector.

example.name: basic_authentication
example.title: API with Basic Authentication
example.description:
Example API using HTTP Basic authentication (username + password).
The password entry has "header": null and "value": null — it is a UI-only field whose value is consumed by the $password placeholder inside the username entry's "Basic base64($username:$password)" template. The engine base64-encodes the interpolated inner expression before writing the Authorization header.
example.note: The connector base64-encodes the username:password combination automatically via the base64(...) template syntax. The password field (header: null, value: null) is collected from the user in the CP4D UI but does not produce a header directly.

example.name: custom_authentication
example.title: API with Custom Authentication Headers
example.description: Some APIs require multiple non-standard authentication headers. Use type "custom" with as many header entries as needed. Each entry maps a connection property to an arbitrary HTTP header.

decision.reason: API uses non-standard headers that don't fit api_key / oauth2 / basic patterns
Each name is the connection-property key CP4D collects from the user AND the $var placeholder used in the value template.
The header value is exactly the connection-property value — no prefix needed.

example.name: authentication_reference
example.title: Authentication Configuration Reference
example.description:
Complete reference for all supported $authentication formats and the $accept_header field.
ACCEPT HEADER: "$accept_header" is an optional top-level field that sets the value of the HTTP Accept header sent with every API request. Defaults to "application/json" when omitted. Use it when the API requires a vendor-specific media type, e.g.: "$accept_header": "application/vnd.dwolla.v1.hal+json" "$accept_header": "application/vnd.github.v3+json" "$accept_header": "application/json" (explicit default)
STRUCTURE — every non-none type uses: "$authentication": { "type": "...", "headers": [ { header-def }, ... ] }
HEADER DEF FIELDS: name — connection-property key; also the $var placeholder in value templates label — human-readable label shown in the CP4D UI description — optional hint text shown in the CP4D UI (can be empty string) masked — true to show the field as password dots in the CP4D UI header — HTTP header name to write into the request (null for UI-only fields) value — value template string (null for UI-only fields)
VALUE TEMPLATE SYNTAX: $name — replaced with the runtime connection-property value for "name" base64(expr) — base64-encodes expr after all $var substitutions; used for Basic auth
UI-ONLY FIELDS: A header entry with "header": null, "value": null is shown in the CP4D UI so the user can provide the credential, but it does not produce an HTTP header directly. Its value is referenced via $name inside another entry's value template. Used for the "password" field in Basic authentication.

example.name: complex_nested_structures
example.title: API with Complex Nested Structures
example.description: Demonstrates handling of nested objects and arrays. Fixed-structure objects use [] suffix for flattening. Arrays and variable-structure objects use VARCHAR.

decision.reason: Fixed-structure nested object with two levels of nesting. Creates columns like: specifications.dimensions.width, specifications.weight.value The materials field (array) within specifications is stored as VARCHAR.
Array of objects - stored as JSON string
decision.wrong: Do NOT create separate reviews table

decision.reason: Array of objects - stored as JSON string

important.rule: Fixed-structure nested objects should use [] suffix for automatic flattening
The connector creates separate columns with dot notation (e.g., object.field)
ALL arrays MUST be mapped as VARCHAR (stored as JSON strings)
Objects with varying structure or containing arrays should use VARCHAR

workflow_example.title: Complete Workflow: Creating Configuration for New API

step.title: User Request
step.user_message: I want to create a connector for the GitHub API to access repository information.

assistant_questions.question: What is the base URL of the GitHub API?
What authentication method does the GitHub API use?
Which specific endpoints do you want to map?
Can you provide an example JSON response from that endpoint?

step.title: Analyze Response
step.analysis: - Endpoint returns single repository object - Has natural unique identifier: "id" (integer) - Contains nested objects: owner, license, permissions - Contains arrays: topics - Mix of data types: strings, integers, booleans, timestamps

step.title: Explain Mapping
step.explanation: - Mapped endpoint to REPOSITORIES table - Used "id" as primary key (INTEGER,$key) - Mapped nested objects (owner, license) as VARCHAR - Mapped arrays (topics) as VARCHAR - Used appropriate types for simple fields

step.title: Confirm and Iterate
step.question: Does this configuration correctly represent the API structure?
step.if_changes_needed: Apply exact changes requested by user

example.name: api_with_pagination
example.title: API with Page-Based Pagination
example.description: GitHub API example demonstrating page-based pagination. Most common pagination type used by REST APIs.
example.configuration: { "$connector_name": "github-api-connector", "$connector_label": "GitHub API", "$connector_description": "Connector for GitHub REST API - provides access to repositories, issues, and more", "$hostname": "https://api.github.com", "$authentication": "oauth2", "$tables": { "REPOSITORIES": { "$path": ["/user/repos"], "$pagination": { "type": "page", "page_param": "page", "limit_param": "per_page", "page_size": 100, "initial_page": 1 }, "id": "INTEGER,$key", "name": "VARCHAR", "full_name": "VARCHAR", "private": "BOOLEAN", "description": "VARCHAR", "html_url": "VARCHAR", "created_at": "TIMESTAMP", "updated_at": "TIMESTAMP", "size": "INTEGER", "stargazers_count": "INTEGER", "language": "VARCHAR" } } }

decision.reason: GitHub API uses page numbers for pagination. Requests look like: ?page=1&per_page=100, ?page=2&per_page=100, etc. Connector automatically fetches all pages until no more data is returned.
GitHub API allows up to 100 items per page - using maximum for better performance

example.name: api_with_cursor_pagination
example.title: API with Cursor-Based Pagination
example.description: Example demonstrating cursor-based pagination where the API provides an opaque token to fetch the next page.

decision.reason: API provides opaque cursor token in response for next page
Actual data array is nested under "data" key in response

example.name: api_with_offset_pagination
example.title: API with Offset-Based Pagination
example.description: Example demonstrating offset-based pagination using numeric offset and limit parameters.

decision.reason: API uses numeric offset for pagination. Requests: ?offset=0&limit=100, ?offset=100&limit=100, etc.
Most APIs start at offset 0 (some may start at 1)

example.name: combined_features
example.title: API with All Features Combined
example.description: Demonstrates using $data_path, $pagination, and object flattening together. Shows how all features work together in a real-world scenario.

decision.reason: Data array is nested: response.result.items
API uses cursor-based pagination. Cursor is at: response.result.pagination.next_cursor
Fixed-structure objects flattened with [] suffix. Creates columns: price.amount, price.currency, dimensions.width, etc.
Array stored as JSON string

example.important: This example shows how $data_path, $pagination, and object flattening work together seamlessly. All three features are independent and can be used in any combination as needed.
